To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a new pruning method that can prune the weights in the network to meet the target resource constraint, which is not possible in previous pruning methods.

we propose a principled framework for channel and spatial pruning that guarantees satisfying the given resource constraints in terms terms of FLOPS and memory, which is not guaranteed by previous works.

(i) the channel-wise pruning approach cannot safely remove inactive channels due to quadratic coupling between channels and (ii) the channel-wise approach cannot guarantee the resource constraints in FLOPs and the memory are satisfied.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two aspects of pruning.
the fundamental problem of channel pruning in convolutional neural networks.
the problem of pruning the redundant weights in the convolutional layers of neural networks to reduce the computational cost and memory usage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a new pruning method which can prune the network in a more efficient manner.
the proposed method is able to achieve competitive pruning results under a given resource constraint.
our method achieves state-of-the-art results on both channel and filter pruning, with the additional benefit of provably preventing inactive weights and meeting the resource constraints.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our proposed framework enables the exact guarantee on resource constraints, and achieves competitive performance compared to the existing methods.

our pruning framework can be used for any CNN architecture, and it provides the exact guarantee for the resource constraints, which is a significant advantage compared to the state-of-the-art pruning methods.

the pruning methods should consider the quadratic coupling between channels and the spatial pruning can further reduce the computational complexity of the pruned network.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we should consider the coupling between the layers and the spatial pruning for the efficient network compression.
the quadratic coupling between channels and the spatial pruning are crucial to achieve the exact guarantee of the pruning objective and resource constraints.
the channel pruning methods are not guaranteed to meet the resource constraints and can be improved by our proposed framework.
